{

  "tools": [
    {
      "id": "admet-predictor",
      "name": "ADMET Property Predictor",
      "description": "Predict ADMET (Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, Toxicity) properties for one or more small molecules using RDKit descriptors and DeepChem pre-trained models. RDKit-computed properties (fast, no model): MW, LogP, TPSA, HBA, HBD, RotBonds, Lipinski Ro5 compliance, Veber compliance. DeepChem model predictions: aqueous solubility (LogS, ESOL model), Caco-2 permeability, human intestinal absorption (HIA), blood-brain barrier penetration (BBB), CYP3A4/2D6/2C9 inhibition flags, hERG cardiotoxicity flag. Molecules are scored with a composite ADMET score (0–1) and ranked. Accepts a SMILES string or a file from molecule-variant-generator output. Returns ranked JSON + CSV. topN limits output to top N molecules by composite score. Runs on ECS Fargate (CPU). Runtime: 5–20 minutes depending on library size.",
      "category": "algorithm",
      "executionMode": "batch",
      "tags": [
        "drug-discovery",
        "medicinal-chemistry",
        "pharmacology"
      ],
      "requiredParameters": []
    },
    {
      "id": "molecular-docking",
      "name": "Molecular Docking",
      "description": "Blind molecular docking of small molecules onto protein targets using DiffDock-L (MIT, MIT/Stanford). Diffusion-based approach: automatically discovers binding pockets without prior knowledge. Success rate: 43% (RMSD <2Å), DockGen generalization benchmark: 22.6% — state-of-the-art blind docking. Generates multiple ranked docking pose candidates with confidence scores. Complements Chai-1 (co-folding from scratch); DiffDock-L docks onto an existing structure. Runs on GPU-accelerated AWS Batch (Spot g5.xlarge). Use for drug discovery: identify binding mode and rank ligand candidates.",
      "category": "algorithm",
      "executionMode": "batch",
      "tags": [
        "structural-biology",
        "drug-discovery"
      ],
      "requiredParameters": [
        "proteinPDB",
        "ligandSMILES"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "molecular-dynamics",
      "name": "Molecular Dynamics Simulation",
      "description": "Run molecular dynamics (MD) simulation to validate protein stability using OpenMM (MIT/LGPL, Stanford). Simulates the protein in explicit water + ions at physiological conditions (300 K, 1 atm, 150 mM NaCl). Validates dynamic stability — ThermoMPNN checks static ΔΔG; OpenMM checks real behaviour over nanoseconds. OpenMM 8 supports ML potentials alongside physics-based force fields. Outputs: trajectory file, RMSD stability plot, per-residue flexibility (RMSF), and average structure PDB. Runtime: ~100–300 ns/day on g5.xlarge (A10G); 50–100 ns sufficient for stability validation. Runs on GPU-accelerated AWS Batch (Spot g5.xlarge). Cost: ~$3–10 per job.",
      "category": "algorithm",
      "executionMode": "batch",
      "tags": [
        "proteomics",
        "structural-biology",
        "protein-engineering"
      ],
      "requiredParameters": [
        "proteinPDB"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "molecule-variant-generator",
      "name": "Molecule Variant Generator",
      "description": "Generate structural variants (analogs) of a query small molecule using RDKit. Applies three complementary strategies: R-group enumeration (replaces substituents with common drug-like groups), bioisostere replacement (classical medicinal chemistry transformations: carboxylic acid → tetrazole, benzene → pyridine, etc.), and fragment growing (extends the scaffold at available attachment points). All variants are automatically filtered by Lipinski Rule of Five (MW ≤ 500, LogP ≤ 5, HBA ≤ 10, HBD ≤ 5) and Veber rules (TPSA ≤ 140, RotBonds ≤ 10) to keep only drug-like candidates. Output: JSON file with up to numVariants molecules, each with SMILES + computed properties (MW, LogP, TPSA, HBA, HBD, RotBonds). Runs on ECS Fargate (CPU). Runtime: 5–15 minutes. Use as the first step of a lead optimization workflow before ADMET prediction and binding affinity ranking.",
      "category": "algorithm",
      "executionMode": "batch",
      "tags": [
        "drug-discovery",
        "medicinal-chemistry",
        "chemical-biology"
      ],
      "requiredParameters": [
        "smiles"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "protein-complex-prediction",
      "name": "Protein Complex Prediction",
      "description": "Predict the 3D structure of multi-molecule complexes using Chai-1 (Apache 2.0, ChaiDiscovery). Co-folds proteins, small molecules, nucleic acids, glycans, and ions simultaneously in one model. Protein-ligand: 77% success rate (vs AlphaFold3 76%). Protein-protein multimers: 75.1% DockQ (beats AlphaFold-Multimer 67.7%). Antibody-antigen: 47.9% DockQ in single-sequence mode. Runs on GPU-accelerated AWS Batch (Spot g5.xlarge). Use when you need multi-molecule complex structure prediction without an AlphaFold3 licence.",
      "category": "algorithm",
      "executionMode": "batch",
      "tags": [
        "proteomics",
        "structural-biology",
        "drug-discovery"
      ],
      "requiredParameters": [
        "sequences"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "protein-sequence-codesign",
      "name": "Protein Sequence Co-design",
      "description": "Generate protein sequence and 3D structure simultaneously using DPLM-2 diffusion model. Performs true joint sequence+structure co-design in a single diffusion pass — no separate inverse folding step. Generates from scratch at a length you choose, and refolds each design with ESMFold to report pLDDT. 650M DPLM-2 model outperforms 3B-scale baselines (ICLR 2025 / ICML 2025 Spotlight). Runs on GPU-accelerated AWS Batch (Spot g5.xlarge). Use for de novo protein generation. It cannot design around a fixed motif; to design a sequence for an existing structure use protein-sequence-infilling.",
      "category": "algorithm",
      "executionMode": "batch",
      "tags": [
        "proteomics",
        "structural-biology",
        "protein-engineering"
      ],
      "requiredParameters": []
    },
    {
      "id": "protein-sequence-generation",
      "name": "Protein Sequence Generation",
      "description": "Generate diverse, natural-looking protein sequences using ProGen2 (Salesforce, BSD-3). Trained on 1 billion protein sequences, ProGen2 produces sequences that respect the evolutionary grammar of real proteins, each with a perplexity score for quality ranking. Conditioning is by SEED SEQUENCE — amino acids the model continues from, such as a known N-terminal fragment of the family you want. A family NAME does not work: ProGen2 has no family vocabulary, so \"GFP\" would be read as the residues Gly-Phe-Pro. Runs on GPU-accelerated AWS Batch (Spot g5.xlarge). Ideal as a fast pre-screening step before expensive GPU design runs.",
      "category": "algorithm",
      "executionMode": "batch",
      "tags": [
        "proteomics",
        "protein-engineering"
      ],
      "requiredParameters": []
    },
    {
      "id": "protein-sequence-infilling",
      "name": "Protein Sequence Infilling",
      "description": "Design new protein sequences for an existing backbone using DPLM-2 inverse folding. Given a PDB structure, generates diverse sequences predicted to fold into that same shape, each scored by refolding it with ESMFold (pLDDT). The design length is set by the input structure. Useful for redesigning or stabilising a protein whose fold you want to keep. NOT motif scaffolding: it cannot hold a few chosen residues fixed while designing the rest, so motifResidues and scaffoldLength are rejected. Runs on GPU-accelerated AWS Batch (Spot g5.xlarge).",
      "category": "algorithm",
      "executionMode": "batch",
      "tags": [
        "proteomics",

        "structurePDB"
